title: Hosted API Demo Chat & Text Generation Basics

Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for chat features in their storefront and is concerned about latency, cost, and SOC2/KMS compliance.

Optimize suggestions: batching, cache, quantization recommendations

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-13 14:00 PDT - Duration ~45m - Attendees: Jordan, Samir, Alex / Maya, Liam, Sofia

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody thanks for joining, um i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll be your AE today, quick agenda - demo of hosted api for chat/text gen, talk streaming and params and retries, quick tour of console and optimize suggestions, and then q&a.
[00:16] Maya: awesome thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we really want to understand expected latencies for our storefront chat and what tradeoffs exist with cost.
[00:25] Jordan: totally - Samir is going to lead the tech bits - Samir over to you.
[00:29] Samir: cool thanks. hi team. quick note my audio might cut in and out, if so i'll paste the snippet after. i'll start with streaming - two common modes we see: server-sent events style streaming (chunked SSE) and HTTP chunk streaming. both let you get partial tokens as they're generated which is great for perceived latency.
[00:48] Liam: is there any difference in throughput or ordering between SSE and chunked?
[00:52] Samir: not really ordering, both guarantee token order. SSE is a bit nicer client-side for browsers, chunked is simpler for backend libs. the important part is we support resumable streams in the SDK and we expose partial deltas in the response so you can render progressively.
[01:08] Alex: also note we expose a "streaming_quality" flag in the Console (demo later) to tune flush frequency - that'll affect cost and cpu.
[01:17] Maya: okay that sounds good.
[01:20] Samir: next, request params - temperature, top_p, max_tokens, presence/ frequency penalties, system messages. small changes to temp/top_p can move you from deterministic to creative. for commerce chat we typically recommend temp 0.0-0.4 and top_p 0.8 but depends on use case.
[01:40] Liam: for structured outputs we should set deterministic, zero temp and use stop tokens?
[01:44] Samir: yep, stop sequences + zero temp and sometimes smaller max_tokens. also you can use function/tool calling for structured outputs but that's another demo.
[01:52] Jordan: quick question from my side - have you guys tried any token limits per request today?
[01:56] Maya: we cap user message length but not sure what model limits we'd hit. sometimes developers send huge context which slows down.
[02:03] Samir: we typically suggest truncation + prefix caching for repeated system prompts. our KV cache, um K-V cache, sorry - the prefix/KV cache - keeps previous system context so you don't re-send large static stuff per request. that reduces tokens and cost.
[02:18] Sofia: on security - is cache encrypted and does it touch customer data?
[02:23] Samir: yes, for hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit, and we provide options to scrub PII from logs. for Private you can bring your KMS and HSM. we'll share the SOC 2 docs after.
[02:34] Jordan: going to demo Postman and the SDK flow - Samir will call the API live.
[02:38] Samir: ok doing a quick code walk. example POST /v1/chat/completions with body: model, messages, temperature, max_tokens, stream true. our SDK wraps the streaming socket and emits events: delta, done, error. here's a typical Node snippet - (paraphrase) const resp = await client.chat.create({model:'redwood-1-small', messages, stream:true}); resp.on('delta', chunk => render(chunk));
[03:03] Liam: you said redwood-1-small - are there multiple variants and cost differences?
[03:07] Samir: yes we have cataloged variants with perf profiles in Console. redwood-1-small is cheaper and lower-latency, redwood-1-large higher quality and cost. Console shows per-token cost estimates.
[03:18] Maya: how do retries work if we hit 429 or 503?
[03:22] Samir: good question - we recommend exponential backoff + jitter for 429 and 503. our SDK has built-in retry helper that retries idempotent requests by default for 429/503 up to configurable limits. for streaming requests we advise the client to resume from last token if you track an idempotency_key. note: some combinations (non-idempotent operations) you may want manual handling.
[03:45] Alex: also rate limits are per-route and exposed in headers; Console will let you set per-route throttling and soft limits to protect downstream.
[03:55] Maya: and what about latency SLOs? we need 200-300ms tail for short chat turns.
[03:59] Samir: if you need aggressive tails go Dedicated with pinned GPUs or use short context models and streaming. for hosted, we typically see median 60-120ms for small models and p95 around 300-800ms depending on region and sequence length. we'll run benchmarks for your prompts.
[04:18] Liam: can you share methodology for those benchmarks?
[04:21] Samir: yes - we'll use a 1-hour sustained QPS test from a region near your users using your prompt set, measure median and p95 token latency and throughput. we'll include caching enabled/disabled, and simulated retries.
[04:34] Jordan: quick Console tour - opening the route dashboard... here you can see per-route token breakdown, cost per call, streaming traces, and the Optimize suggestions panel.
[04:45] Alex: Optimize will surface batching and caching opportunities - for example it might say: bundle small requests within 50ms window to save 22% token overhead, or enable prefix KV cache for repeated system prompts. it also suggests quantization only for Dedicated/Private variants.
[05:03] Maya: that batching - will that add latency? our customers expect snappy replies.
[05:08] Samir: there is a tradeoff. Optimize shows estimated latency impact and cost savings; you can pick a batching policy (max wait 20ms, 50ms, etc). often a 10-20ms wait yields significant cost savings and negligible UX impact when streaming.
[05:23] Sofia: security again - can we ship logs to our SIEM and are there audit trails per token request?
[05:28] Jordan: yes we export audit logs and webhook them to your SIEM; Console also keeps per-request tracing and you can redact token payloads in logs. we'll send the security pack.
[05:39] Liam: about idempotency keys - how do we handle partial streamed responses on retry?
[05:44] Samir: best practice is to store a client-side last_token_offset and resume with an idempotency key plus a resume cursor - our SDK supports resume for chunked streams; otherwise you re-request and stitch. we'll show an example in the follow-up doc.
[05:59] Maya: okay good. pricing question - is streaming charged per token consumed or per second?
[06:04] Jordan: per-token for generation and per-embedding unit separately; streaming doesn't add extra charge other than tokens. we show estimated per-call cost in Console.
[06:12] Liam: any guidance for mixed workloads (short chat + longer summarization)?
[06:16] Samir: route to different model variants by policy - low-latency small model for short Qs, larger model for batch offline summarization. Smart routing can fallback when capacity constrained.
[06:28] Maya: procurement timeline - we need procurement OK by end of month. open to pilot first.
[06:33] Jordan: great - pilot + benchmark is perfect.
[06:36] Alex: quick demo of retry headers in Console - you can simulate 429s and see the SDK helper's retry attempts. also we surface 429/503 counts in the trace table.
[06:49] Lily (note: misattributed speaker, auto): [inaudible]
[06:52] Samir: haha not Lily - ignore that.
[06:55] Maya: couple of clarifying Qs - if we want on-prem later how much work to migrate from hosted?
[07:01] Samir: migration path is supported: same API surface, pinned model versions, export of route config. Dedicated is intermediate for committed capacity. Private/on-prem has additional network setup and requires a plan for data egress, but your prompts and client code can remain nearly identical.
[07:18] Sofia: do you support bringing our own KMS?
[07:22] Alex: yes for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer managed KMS and a bring-your-own-KMS option for enterprise tiers.
[07:31] Liam: is there any change in model quantization between hosted and dedicated?
[07:35] Samir: we may run different quantized kernels on Dedicated to squeeze more throughput; Console's Optimize will call out recommended quantization profiles per workload. quality regressions are tracked in evals.
[07:47] Maya: ok that's helpful. can you recap next steps?
[07:51] Jordan: sure - Samir will run a 1-hour benchmark with your prompts and share numbers; I'll send pricing and the SOC2/KMS docs; Alex will prep a short Console video on throttling and resume. we'll target those items by the dates I sent.
[08:10] Liam: thanks everyone - we'll share prompt set by Tuesday.
[08:15] Maya: one last thing - do you do token-level cost alerts?
[08:18] Alex: we have per-route cost alerts you can set in Console and webhook to billing channels.
[08:24] Jordan: ok wrapping up. thanks all - we'll follow up via email.
